newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB no comment on India wheat, confirms Egypt deal.
newsitem.headline: AWB no comment on India wheat, confirms Egypt deal.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) would not comment at present on wheat sales to India, Nigel Officer, AWB general manager international, said on Thursday.
Officer was responding to a question from Reuters on whether the AWB had sold one million tonnes of wheat to India.
Officer confirmed, however, that Egypt had bought 100,000 tonnes of Australian wheat for May and June delivery.
The AWB was still negotiating to sell a further 50,000 tonnes of wheat to Egypt, he said.
Egypt had specified either Australian or U.S. origin wheat for this component of its tender.
Speculation has been high among European and U.S. grains traders in recent weeks that Australia had carried out a further one million tonne wheat sale to India.
Last December the AWB announced it had struck a one million tonne wheat sale to India for January-February delivery.
In February this year the AWB also announced that it had sold 200,000 tonnes of wheat to India for March delivery.
Last December the Indian government authorised the import of up to two million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 (April to March) to increase supplies and check rising domestic prices.
In recent weeks European traders have said shipment dates for Australia's expected new one million tonne sale to India were August and October for 250,000 tonnes each and December for 500,000 tonnes.
U.S. and European traders have said the deals were done at US$154.25 to $155 per tonne, fob.
